title: A randomized, double-blind, controlled three-arm trial evaluating transversus abdominis plane block compared with wound infiltration and standard opioid-based treatment for perioperative analgesia in robot-assisted radical prostatectomy
summary:
Pain can occur after robot-assisted removal of the prostate despite the small skin incisions. It is usually treated with several types of pain medication, including opioids. This study investigates whether adding local or regional anaesthesia can reduce opioid requirements during surgery and improve recovery afterwards.

The study plans to enrol 213 adult men with prostate cancer who are scheduled for this operation. Participants will be randomly assigned with equal probability to one of three groups. One group will receive an ultrasound-guided injection of local anaesthetic around nerves supplying the abdominal wall, called a TAP block, after induction of general anaesthesia. A second group will receive local anaesthetic injections into the surgical wounds. The third group will receive standard pain treatment without an additional local or regional anaesthetic procedure. All groups will receive standardized general anaesthesia and pain treatment, with additional pain medication available whenever needed.

The main comparison is the amount of opioid medication administered during surgery, from skin incision to skin closure. Further assessments include postoperative opioid use, pain intensity, perceived recovery, time spent in the recovery room, time to the first bowel movement and length of hospital stay. Questionnaires will be completed in the recovery room and during the first two days after surgery; hospital discharge will also be documented. No additional outpatient follow-up visits are planned. Participants will not be told their group allocation during the study. Participation is voluntary and may be discontinued at any time without affecting medical care.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Histologically confirmed prostate cancer with an indication for elective robot-assisted radical prostatectomy.
• Planned surgery under general anaesthesia according to the standardized institutional protocol.
• ASA physical status I–III and BMI ≤ 40 kg/m².
• Capacity to provide independent informed consent and written informed consent after comprehensive study information.
• Sufficient German language proficiency to fully understand the study information, questions and answers, and written consent.
• Expected ability to cooperate with postoperative assessments using the NRS and QoR-15.
Exclusion criteria:
• Lack of capacity to provide informed consent, including cognitive impairment preventing informed consent.
• Contraindications to TAP block: allergy or hypersensitivity to amide-type local anaesthetics; infection at the injection site; severe coagulation disorder or therapeutic anticoagulation contraindicating regional blockade; local anatomical conditions preventing safe performance.
• Known intolerance to medications for general anesthesia.
• Chronic high-dose opioid therapy.
• ASA physical status IV or higher.
• Severe hepatic or renal impairment relevant to the pharmacokinetics of opioids or local anaesthetics.
• Severe neurological or psychiatric disorders affecting pain processing or study adherence.
• Extensive previous abdominal wall surgery potentially altering the anatomical spread of the TAP block, as judged by the surgeon or anaesthesiologist.
• Concurrent participation in another interventional clinical study that may influence pain treatment or perioperative medication.
• Non-elective surgery.
